title: Black and white with real colour filters
body: Black-and-white films used to be a plain grey conversion. On 16 September they got a channel mixer, so each mono film behaves as if it were shot through a colour filter: a red filter darkens a blue sky, a green one lightens leaves.

images.alt: The lake in colour, in Silver Mono, and in Scarlet Sky Mono, where the sky and water turn much darker.
images.caption: Silver Mono is close to a neutral conversion. Scarlet Sky Mono carries a red filter, so the blue sky and water drop toward black while the white buildings stay bright.
